name: rating
purpose: Rating is a row of stars that picks a whole score from 1 to `max` (5 by default), the way a customer rates a support conversation (CSAT) or a product review. It renders as a native radio group, one radio per star named "1 star" … "5 stars", so it is one tab stop, the arrow keys move the score and the value posts with a form. With `readonly` it becomes a display of a score, including a fractional average rounded to the nearest half star (4.5 shows four and a half stars), announced as one image ("Rated 4.5 out of 5").
useWhen: Ask a customer to rate a support conversation, an answer or a resolved ticket on a 1-to-5 scale (customer satisfaction, CSAT): the star they pick is the answer, sent on `select`.
Collect a star score in a review or feedback form, inside a `Field` with a label, a description and a required error.
Show a stored score or an average of scores as stars in a ticket, a table cell or a review list (`readonly`).
avoidWhen: A good / bad (thumbs up / thumbs down) answer → use `ToggleGroup` with two options, or `ChatMessageFeedback` under an AI answer.
A score on a scale wider than 10 or a continuous value → use `Slider` or `NumberInput`.
A choice between named options (plans, channels) → use `RadioGroup`.
A score shown as a number or a bar (NPS breakdown, a meter) → use `StatTile` or `Progress`.
related: `radio-group` — the same native radio pattern, for picking one labelled option instead of a score.
`toggle-group` — two or three compact options such as good / bad.
`chat-message-feedback` — thumbs up / thumbs down under an AI chat answer.
`field` — wraps the rating with its label, description and error; the label names the group.
`slider` — a number on a wide or continuous scale.
bestPractices: Name the group: put it in a `Field` with a `Field.Title`, or set `aria-label` on the root ("Rate this conversation").
Keep `max` at 5 for satisfaction and reviews; scales above 5 are hard to tell apart at a glance.

When the score is the whole answer (a CSAT question), send it on `select` and add no Send button: the pick is the submit, as in Intercom and Help Scout. Then replace the stars with a short thank-you ("Thanks, your rating was sent.") in a `role="status"` element and move focus to it. A comment, when you ask for one, comes after the score is already saved.
Start empty (`0`) when you ask for a rating, so nobody submits a score they did not choose; set `required` when the score is mandatory.
Set `clearable` when a score is optional, so a person can take it back with the keyboard and a screen reader, not only by reloading.
Show averages with `readonly`; print the count of ratings beside it in text ("4.5 · 128 reviews"), the stars do not carry it.
Do not put a rating in a dense table row as an input; show it `readonly` and edit it in a dialog or a detail page.

props.name: max
props.doc: Number of stars, the highest score. Rounded to a whole number and kept between 1 and 10.

props.name: size
props.doc: Star size: 16, 20 or 24 px glyphs in 24, 28 or 32 px targets. `RatingSize`, exported.

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name shared by every star radio; the score submits under it. Empty uses a generated name so the radios still group.

props.name: readonly
props.doc: Shows the score instead of asking for it: no radios, the value rounded to the nearest half star, announced as one image.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables every star and the clear button; the row shows at 50 % opacity with a not-allowed cursor.

props.name: required
props.doc: Requires a score: sets `aria-required` on the group and `required` on the radios, so a native form blocks an empty submit.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the rating invalid: sets `aria-invalid` on the group and draws the empty stars in the danger mark colour.

props.name: clearable
props.doc: Shows a clear button after the stars that resets the score to 0 and moves focus to the first star. Not shown while `readonly`.
